This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail relating to FIR No.320/2022 dated (not mentioned) registered at Police Station M.P. Nagar, District Bhopal, for the offence under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code.

entities.text: Police Station M.P. Nagar, District Bhopal
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is in jail since 29.04.2023.

He submits that as per case of prosecution, the applicant along with other accomplice impersonating themselves to be the employees of Central Bank of India and collected Rs.20 lacs from the complainants under the garb of getting their loan sanctioned, but when nothing was done and the complainants found themselves to be cheated, they lodged a report and on their complaint offence got registered against the applicant and other co-accused persons.

He submits that the applicant has been made accused Abhay Shrivastava vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123529756/
1 on the basis of memorandum of other co-accused persons.

entities.text: Abhay Shrivastava vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He submits that facing the similar allegations, the main accused namely Sanjay Sinha has been granted bail by this Court vide order dated 06.02.2023 passed in M.Cr.C. No.1616 of 2023.
He submits that when the main accused has been granted bail, then the present applicant who was made accused on the basis of memorandum may also be enlarged on bail on the ground of parity.

On the other hand, learned Panel Lawyer has opposed the prayer of bail and submitted that the present applicant cannot claim parity with that of Sanjay Sinha for the reason that he was not identified by the complainants whereas the present applicant was identified by the complainant namely Laik Shah.
He has also submitted that in maximum documents, the photograph of present applicant namely Abhay Shrivastava was found.
He has also submitted that the applicant was absconded and arrested later on and his custody period is also too short, therefore, he is not entitled to be enlarged on bail.

Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, perusal of case diary and also the order passed in M.Cr.C. No.1616 of 2023, I am of the opinion that the applicant cannot claim parity with that of Sanjay Sinha who has been granted bail for the reason that he was not identified by the complainants whereas the present applicant was identified by one of the complainants and further looking to his custody period which is too short, at this stage, I am not inclined to enlarge the present applicant on bail.

(SANJAY DWIVEDI) JUDGE Devashish DEVASHISH MISHRA 2023.06.21 11:51:24 +05'30'
